evidence: Receiving DO2 50.2h=1.90, 50.4h=2.17, 51.0h=1.90, 52.0h=1.60 mg/L — at/below the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Pre-crash receiving DO2 ~11.4 mg/L at 50.0h; ~85% step drop not seen in any source batch
Receiving P assay: 3.06 g/L at 48h — batch was on a trajectory comparable to healthy source batches before the oxygen deficit
Source batches maintained DO2 8–13 mg/L throughout with no comparable crash, indicating receiving-specific oxygen supply/demand mismatch
Action bounds: combined=[0.8, 1.15]; stop=null; measurement menu turnaround 4h under KEEP
submission.rationale: At t=50.2h the receiving vessel's DO2 collapsed from ~11.4 mg/L to ~1.9 mg/L and has drifted to 1.6 mg/L by 52h, below the 2.0 mg/L oxygen minimum — an active oxygen-constraint violation. This deviation is unique to the receiving process (all three source batches held DO2 in the 8–13 mg/L range at comparable times), so it reflects a receiving-side oxygen supply/demand imbalance, not normal batch behavior. An extra product assay (4h turnaround, KEEP meanwhile) would leave the vessel in violation for at least 4 more hours and does not inform oxygen dynamics. Increase_air alone (×1.15) provides only ~15% more oxygen transfer against a ~85% DO2 deficit and is unlikely to restore compliance. Strong_feed_reduction (×0.6 feed) sacrifices substantially more product mass than needed for a moderate demand reduction, and stop yields zero counted production. The combined intervention (feed ×0.8, air ×1.15) reduces oxygen demand by 20% while boosting transfer by 15%, with a high probability of restoring DO2 above 2.0 mg/L while retaining most of the batch's productive capacity and the product mass already accumulated (P ≈ 3.06 g/L at 48h).
submission.uncertainty: The hidden receiving kinetics are unknown; it is uncertain whether a 15% air increase plus 20% feed reduction fully restores DO2 above 2.0 mg/L, since the deficit is large. There is a tradeoff risk: the 20% feed cut reduces near-term product accumulation relative to KEEP if the DO2 crash were transient or sensor-related. No model tool was available to quantify recovery; the choice relies on the direction and bounded magnitudes of the two levers versus the observed deficit.
